topics.topic: Billing-data operation behavior when required fiscal or personal values are absent
questions: What does the billing-data read return when the customer exists but lacks a tax id, legal name or required person name?
What does the billing-data operation do when a required document value is absent?
What observable result occurs when PresuPro requests billing data for a customer whose tax id or legal name was never recorded?

quotes: the Customer with the identity (`customer_ref`) Registry minted for it (R0-16), its kind — person or company — its contact data (R0-06, R0-37) and, when given, its fiscal data: tax id (NIF/NIE/CIF) and legal name (R0-80)
the customer named by `customer_ref`: kind, tax id and legal name — for a person, the full name as on the document — never its contact data
judgement.divergence: One implementation returns an incomplete or nullable billing-data result when fiscal values are absent; another refuses the operation. PresuPro notices whether it receives data or an error when issuing a document.
judgement.why: The promised billing read has no stated outcome for customers whose optional fiscal values were never recorded.

topics.topic: When the one-home rule becomes mandatory during migration and which temporary copies may remain
questions: When does the one-home rule become an actual product invariant, and what guarantees apply while other services and legacy instances still keep copies?
Is the one-home rule an invariant required when production starts, or a migration target under which named temporary copies may remain?
Is the one-home rule an immediate invariant of production, or a target invariant that temporarily permits the existing named service copies after production starts?

quotes: Registry is the one home of a customer's personal data: no other service keeps a customer record or a copy of its values, except as fixed in a document it issued and in Client Portal's offline projection (R0-80).

Production Registry starts without waiting for the other services. From its start Registry holds the customer's personal data as R0-80 says and gives each service what it needs to stop keeping copies. Each service removes its own customer records and copies in its own case — PresuPro's project snapshots and database backups, Cabinet's package of projects, the legacy instances once retired (R0-79). Until each has, the governance's records of processing list the copies that remain, with their service and the change that removes them.
judgement.why: The first passage states that no other service keeps copies, while the second permits acknowledged copies to remain after production starts.

topics.topic: Whether the one-home rule covers all identifying object characteristics or only addresses
questions: Does the one-home/no-copy rule cover every identifying characteristic of an object, or only its address?
Are identifying characteristics also forbidden from being kept by other services, or does the one-home restriction apply only to the address?
Does the prohibition on copies outside Registry cover all object identifying characteristics as well as the address?

quotes: Personal data — the customer's contact and fiscal data and the object's address and identifying characteristics are `personal_data`; a project's identity is not anonymous by itself (R0-26).
A customer's living personal data — name, contact data, tax id (NIF/NIE/CIF), legal name — and the object's address are held only by Registry.
judgement.divergence: One implementation forbids other services from persisting every identifying object characteristic; another forbids only copies of the address. Consumer services and the governance owner notice which characteristics remain in external stores.
judgement.why: The text classifies identifying characteristics as personal data but names only the address in the one-home storage rule.
judgement.failure: the quoted passage of a consequential gap is not found verbatim in the texts

topics.topic: Which customer and fiscal fields survive customer erasure
questions: Does customer erasure remove tax id, legal name, kind, restriction and relationship-end state, or do any of them survive?
Does customer erasure also remove tax id, legal name, kind, restriction state and relationship-ended state, or do any of them survive?
When customer data is erased, are kind, tax id and legal name also removed, or do any of them survive?

judgement.why: P9 already judged the same question on the same passages: only the Customer identity and erased fact survive.

precedent.topic: Customer fields removed or retained after erasure
quotes:
Erasing a customer's contact data (R0-06) is the end of its record: the
Customer keeps its identity and the fact that it was erased, and projects keep
naming it. There is no action that deletes a Customer whole.
precedent.why: Because the erased Customer keeps only its identity and erased fact, kind, tax id and legal name do not survive.

topics.topic: Concurrency preconditions and stale-revision behavior for mutations
questions: Which of these mutations must carry the current project or customer revision, and what happens on a stale revision?
Which revision or concurrency token must accompany each owner mutation outside Project and Customer, and what is the failure when it is stale?

judgement.why: P7 already assigns mutation revision requirements, advancement, stale-input behavior and idempotent behavior to State 2.

precedent.topic: Revision requirements and behavior for mutations and idempotent no-ops
quotes:
Every change carries CSRF protection and
is validated on the server; a change made against an older revision is refused
(R0-35).

A project, a customer and an object carry a revision that every accepted change
moves. A change states the revision it was made against; a change against an
older revision is refused and nothing changes. Every change is atomic.

Narrowed by R0-45: the object has no revision of its own; a change of it moves
the project's.
the session's granted project ids, its active project if any, whether it has a pending request, and the access version — no `personal_data` value (R0-32, R0-46, R0-64)
precedent.why: Mapping expected versions to mutations, defining version advancement and specifying stale or idempotent behavior are rules and required tests owned by State 2.

topics.topic: How anonymisation handles retained uninspected artifact pointer values
questions: How can anonymisation guarantee that retained pointer values do not identify a person when Registry never inspects them?
How can anonymisation guarantee that no personal or re-identifying value remains when `uri` or `payload_ref` is retained without inspection?

judgement.why: P2 already answers the conditions under which identifiers and pointers may remain in an anonymised project.

precedent.topic: Requirements for retained identifiers and pointers in anonymised projects
quotes: A project's technical identity, status and artifact pointers are kept only where it is shown that they no longer allow re-identification and a justified purpose for keeping them is recorded; `validate` then answers `archived`. Otherwise the record is deleted whole, and `validate` answers `not_found`.
Narrowed by R0-60: the owner chooses between the two when erasing; the showing and the purpose are recorded in the governance.
precedent.why: Retention is permitted only after a governance-recorded showing that the retained identity and pointers no longer allow re-identification; otherwise the project is deleted whole.

topics.topic: Whether consumers may persist a potentially personal project display name
questions: May a consumer persist a project display name even when it contains a person's name, or must persistent snapshots omit or constrain it?
May a consumer persist `display name` when it can contain a person's name, or must persisted snapshots omit it unless some concrete rule makes it non-personal?

quotes: A consumer's kept snapshot holds identity — id, display name, status, `customer_ref` — never a personal value such as the address.
Registry cannot tell a person's name from any other word, so the agent projection leaves out the project's display name: the agent works by the project's id.
judgement.why: The snapshot promise permits retaining the display name while asserting it is never personal, but the other passage says Registry cannot determine whether that display name is a person's name.

topics.topic: Whether restriction blocks fiscal and billing-data use as well as contact-data processing
questions: Does restriction block fiscal/billing-data reads as well as contact-data processing?
Does restriction block use of fiscal billing data too, or only contact data?

quotes: A restriction (R0-51, R0-55) covers the customer's contact data; the object's address stays project data and is served as before.
unknown customer refused; an erased or restricted customer refused (R0-65); any other caller refused
judgement.why: One passage limits the restriction to contact data, while the billing-data operation refuses fiscal-data access solely because the customer is restricted.

topics.topic: Whether the one-time migration import is fixed to the named projects or owner-selected
questions: Is the one allowed production import restricted to the two named project ids, or may the owner choose a different subset when executing it?
Is the import input fixed to exactly the two named project ids, or may the owner choose a different subset from the VPS when performing the import?

quotes: The only source is the Registry on the VPS, imported once. At the import the owner picks any of its projects; the owner's choice of 2026-10-27 is "Comunidad de Propietarios C/ del Progreso 140" (`37241411-f235-4a32-bb31-9629d1079dd2`) and the project of Uliana Kolpacheva (`c276a851-9b8a-44c7-bbf7-20e363b0ad5f`), under the ids Client Portal already names.
judgement.divergence: One implementation accepts only the two recorded project ids; another lets the owner select any VPS subset when executing the one import. The owner notices which projects the interface permits importing.
judgement.why: The passage both grants selection at import time and records a specific prior choice without saying whether that choice is binding.

topics.topic: Which accepted, refused, and state-changing actions produce audit entries
questions: Which exact state-changing primary actions create audit entries?
Exactly which accepted and refused actions create audit entries?

judgement.why: P10 already assigns exact audit coverage, including refused changes, to State 2.

precedent.topic: Audit coverage, including whether refused changes are logged
quotes:
Registry records only significant changes of state: changes to projects and
customer records, granting and revoking an agent session's projects,
restricting processing and lifting it, and erasures and anonymisations. Ordinary reads, agent calls and the inner steps of flows
are not recorded in Registry; security events of the infrastructure are
handled by the infrastructure, outside Registry.

- **Audit.** A minimal log of significant changes of state (R0-58): time, the
  acting principal (owner, which service, agent through Kernel), the change,
  the project or customer, the outcome, the contract and release version, and
  a confirmation id where the owner confirmed.
precedent.why: The exact event-selection and outcome-recording criteria are operational rules and required tests owned by State 2.

topics.topic: Which document lifecycle event permits retaining fixed personal values
questions: Which document states qualify for the persistence exception, and what happens to drafts, previews, regenerated documents and withdrawn publications?
What observable event makes a document eligible to retain fixed personal values, and can drafts, regenerated versions or unsent estimates use the exception?

quotes: A document a service issues — an invoice, an estimate sent to the customer, a publication in Client Portal — fixes the values of its date and is kept under the lawful ground and period the governance records (R0-60); an erasure in Registry does not rewrite it.
The documents a service issues, with the customer's values fixed at their date (R0-80).
judgement.divergence: One implementation permits persistence as soon as a draft or preview is generated; another permits it only after an externally observable issue, send or publication event. The issuing service, customer and governance owner notice which document versions retain personal values.
judgement.why: The persistence exception depends on a document being issued, but the product text does not name the action or observable event that makes it issued.

topics.topic: Which events increment session access version and whether it is a concurrency token
questions: Which state transitions increment the access version, and can callers use it as a concurrency precondition?
Which events change a session's access version, and does replacing or clearing a pending request count?

judgement.why: P6 already assigns the meaning, transition rules and concurrency role of the access version to State 2.

precedent.topic: Meaning, concurrency role, and mutation rules of the agent-session access version
quotes: the session's granted project ids, its active project if any, whether it has a pending request, and the access version — no `personal_data` value (R0-32, R0-46, R0-64)
A change states the revision it was made against; a change against an older revision is refused and nothing changes. Every change is atomic.
precedent.why: Mutation preconditions, version-transition rules and stale-input behavior are rules and required tests owned by State 2.

topics.topic: Which owner-interface requests and response data are allowed before authentication
questions: Which owner-interface requests, if any, may answer before authentication, and what may those answers contain?
Which owner-interface requests, if any, may be answered before an owner session exists so that sign-in can occur?

quotes: No operation of Registry answers an unauthenticated caller. The owner signs in to the owner interface (R0-30); each service — PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel — holds its own service token, which names it and the operations and highest disclosure class it may use.
There is one human principal, the owner. The owner signs in to the owner interface with the owner credential and gets a protected session; the session and its expiry belong to State 2.
judgement.why: No unauthenticated owner-interface request may answer; the sign-in request is authenticated with the owner credential and then creates the protected session.

topics.topic: Which person-name field billing reads may disclose despite contact-data restrictions
questions: Is a person's document name billing data that PresuPro may receive, or contact data that no service may receive?
Which stored field supplies a person's full name to the billing-data operation, and may the operation disclose the ordinary customer name despite the rule that contact data reaches the owner alone?

quotes: the customer named by `customer_ref`: kind, tax id and legal name — for a person, the full name as on the document — never its contact data
Name, phone, e-mail and language are all the customer's contact data: personal data, readable by staff only (R0-09), and erasable as a whole.
A service whose token allows it — today PresuPro, to issue documents — reads the customer's billing data; contact data still reaches the owner alone.
judgement.divergence: One implementation returns the ordinary customer name as the person's document name; another returns only a distinct fiscal legal name and refuses or leaves it absent when that field is missing. PresuPro and the customer notice which name appears on the issued document.
judgement.why: The output promises a person's full name without identifying a non-contact source, while ordinary customer name is expressly contact data that services may not receive.

topics.topic: Which personal and project fields Client Portal may persist offline
questions: Which exact Registry fields may Client Portal persist in its offline projection, particularly customer name, contact fields, project display name, address and object characteristics?
May Client Portal's offline projection contain the customer's name or other contact data, or must those values be excluded despite being visible in the customer's cabinet?

judgement.why: P3 already assigns the exact fields permitted in Client Portal's offline projection to State 6.

precedent.topic: Which personal values Client Portal may retain in its offline projection
quotes:
Client
Portal's offline projection (R0-39) is Portal's publication to the customer:
it holds only what the customer's own cabinet shows, never a tax id, and is the
one kept copy this rule admits besides issued documents.

What the
projection holds and how old it may be is Portal's design, bounded by the
disclosure classes its token allows (R0-26).
precedent.why: The exact fields permitted in the persisted Portal projection are an output-contract and schema question owned by State 6, and the text expressly assigns the projection's contents to Portal's design.
